## a962b3033531

**Reproduced shortcut/domain gap: walls can be ignored on the selected generator
support.** The pinned audited generator SHA-256 is
`08f2a7bdc29e1f3c31a1a8c99c3eeb2047f3a0f3d18e10eae4a911996246cfe8`.
The default generator always creates one rectangular room using only an outer
color-5 border; it never emits an internal partition. Consequently a rival that
fills every zero by the globally nearest seed, ignoring room connectivity,
fits the whole selected default support.

A saved 7×9 two-room input with an internal color-5 wall is valid for the
canonical rule but intentionally lies outside the selected generator's documented
default domain. Supported Racket apply executed rule hash `6b26f6d5b032` and
disagreed with the global rival at 9 cells. At witness cell `[1,3]`, room-aware
authority returns color 2 while the global rival returns color 8.

Evidence: `checks/audit-a962b3033531/internal-wall-input.json`,
`authority-output.json`, `global-nearest-rival.json`,
`room-vs-global-metadata.json`, and `racket.json`. Command from `packet_root`:
`python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply a962b3033531 --input ../checks/audit-a962b3033531/internal-wall-input.json --out ../checks/audit-a962b3033531/racket.json`.
I left the audit target unchanged as required.
